articles.title: Reassessing the Kocher Criteria: A Prospective Evaluation of Diagnostic Performance in Pediatric Musculoskeletal Infection.
articles.authors: Rogie GA, Barksdale EM 3rd, Braithwaite HC 4th, Mo M, Clever D, Enata N, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 0 to 18 years presenting with suspected musculoskeletal infection
articles.sample_size: 102 patients (42 with transient synovitis, 30 with osteomyelitis, 30 with septic arthritis)
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic performance of Kocher criteria and inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, white blood cell count) in differentiating septic arthritis from transient synovitis and osteomyelitis
articles.take_home: The Kocher criteria work moderately well to distinguish septic arthritis from transient synovitis but cannot reliably tell septic arthritis apart from bone infection due to overlapping symptoms and blood test results. These criteria should guide doctors towards ordering advanced imaging rather than being used as a definitive rule for surgery.

articles.title: Radiologic Sequelae of Pediatric Septic Arthritis of the Shoulder: A Retrospective Series and Proposed Classification.
articles.authors: Agarwal A, Iqbal MZ, Khurana S, Gupta M, Sahoo S, Deep A
articles.population: Children treated for septic arthritis of the shoulder
articles.outcomes: Long-term radiologic sequelae classified into 4 types: complete recovery, epiphyseal irregularity, physeal arrest or bar formation, and articular destruction
articles.take_home: Septic arthritis of the shoulder in young children often causes permanent bone growth problems, with damage to the growth plate being the most common long-term effect. Babies and children with widespread bone infections are at highest risk of severe complications.

articles.title: Management of chronic monteggia fractures with ulnar osteotomy, external fixation and gradual closed reduction of radial head.
articles.authors: Liu S, Zhu J, Xin Z
articles.population: Patients aged over 10 years with chronic Monteggia fractures (missed dislocation for over 1 year or with radial head deformities)
articles.outcomes: Recurrent radial head dislocation, pin tract infections, elbow flexion and supination range of motion, radiographic changes
articles.take_home: A surgical approach combining ulnar osteotomy, external fixation and gradual closed reduction successfully treated chronic Monteggia fractures in this small group, with no patients experiencing recurrent dislocation and most maintaining good elbow function, though some developed minor complications like pin tract infections.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Outcomes of Intraoperative Neuromonitoring in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: A Comprehensive Analysis of 5,206 Patients.
articles.authors: CreveCoeur TS, Samdani AF, Schupper AJ, Ishmael TG, Miyanji F, Shah SA, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis from prospective database
articles.population: Adolescent patients with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing spinal fusion surgery
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative neuromonitoring alert rates by curve type; risk factors for alerts; neurologic deficits; spinal curve correction at 2-year follow-up
articles.take_home: During scoliosis surgery, warning signals from nerve monitoring occurred in 5% of patients, mainly those with larger curves and certain curve patterns. These alerts led to interventions such as raising blood pressure, and permanent nerve damage occurred in fewer than 1% of patients. Despite the alerts, patients achieved similar improvements in their spinal curves after 2 years.

articles.title: Perspectives of patients and families impacted by developmental dysplasia of the hip.
articles.authors: De Silva D, Zomar BO, Webber DR, Mulpuri K, Schaeffer EK
articles.study_type: Qualitative study using focus groups and thematic content analysis
articles.population: Patients with developmental dysplasia of the hip and their caregivers
articles.outcomes: Identified key themes including patient anxiety, activity limitation, long-term effects, lack of involvement in decisions, and caregiver burden; highlighted need for better information and support services
articles.take_home: Patients and families affected by developmental dysplasia of the hip experience anxiety about medical visits, feel limited in their activities, and often lack involvement in treatment decisions. The findings will help healthcare providers develop more patient-centred care and research that addresses what matters most to patients and families.

articles.title: Low Sensitivity of Neurological Examination, Curve Laterality, and Thoracic Kyphosis for Detecting Chiari I Malformation and Syrinx in Operative Pediatric Scoliosis.
articles.authors: Budd LR, Strahle JM, Vorhies JS, Kelly BA, Chen L, Tang SY, et al.
articles.population: Children with scoliosis undergoing surgery who had Chiari I malformation and/or syrinx
articles.sample_size: 47 patients (4 with Chiari I malformation only, 23 with syrinx only, 20 with both)
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity of abnormal neurological examination, left-sided thoracic curve, and thoracic hyperkyphosis for detecting Chiari I malformation and syrinx
articles.take_home: Standard screening signs like abnormal neurological exams, left-sided curves, or excessive thoracic kyphosis only picked up 66% of patients with these conditions. About one in three children with Chiari I malformation or syrinx had completely normal examination findings and normal spine curvature, suggesting surgeons should consider MRI screening more broadly before scoliosis surgery rather than relying only on these classic warning signs.

articles.title: A Novel Flexor Tendon Reconstruction Technique in Children: A Potential Solution for a Rare Problem.
articles.authors: Mazurek T, Zerdzicki K, Napora J, Ceynowa M, Korolkiewicz PK
articles.population: Paediatric cadaveric specimens aged 10 to 14 years
articles.sample_size: 9 digits from paediatric donors and 9 palmaris longus tendons from adult cadavers
articles.outcomes: Ultimate failure load, elongation under 20 N load, elongation at failure, and failure mechanisms of the tendon fixation construct
articles.take_home: A new technique for reattaching tendon grafts in children undergoing flexor tendon reconstruction showed adequate strength and stability to allow early active movement during healing. The main weakness was that the anchor tended to pull out of the soft paediatric bone rather than the suture failing.

articles.title: Assessment and management of torsional malalignment in paediatric patients with patellofemoral joint instability.
articles.authors: Accadbled F, Cheok T, Martinel V, Rawat J
articles.population: Children and adolescents with patellofemoral joint instability
articles.outcomes: Assessment methods for torsional malalignment; imaging evaluation; surgical management outcomes
articles.take_home: Torsional malalignment (abnormal twisting of the thighbone or shinbone) is often missed but contributes to knee instability in children. Correcting this malalignment with surgery, when appropriate, can improve knee stability and reduce the chance of treatment failure.

articles.title: Spinal Fusion in Prader-Willi Syndrome: Early Radiographic Outcomes and Complications With a Subset Analysis of Two-year Follow-up in a Multicenter Cohort.
articles.authors: Lobato AG, Andras L, Vaughan M, Ramo BA, McQuerry JL, Huser AJ, et al.
articles.population: Children with Prader-Willi syndrome undergoing spinal fusion
articles.outcomes: Radiographic correction of scoliosis and kyphosis, perioperative complications, unplanned return to operating room, functional outcomes measured by EOSQ-24
articles.take_home: Spinal fusion in children with Prader-Willi syndrome effectively corrects spine deformity and improves function, but carries a higher-than-average risk of complications and early reoperation, particularly in children with higher body mass index.
